name: Haze Nygaard
location: Geartown, beneath the Kessler Interchange overpass, near Damen and Armitage
description:
Haze Nygaard is small, dense, and permanent-looking, like a boulder that has decided to become a person. Her dark skin is mapped with the small scars of a lifetime handling sharp metal, and her left arm from the elbow down is a functional prosthetic she salvaged and assembled herself over the course of a decade — mismatched parts from at least four different manufacturers, currently painted a deep burgundy with yellow geometric lines her grandchildren helped design. She wears magnification goggles pushed up on her forehead at all times, leaving permanent red rings around her eyes. Her natural hair is cropped close and gone entirely silver.

She knows the value of everything. Not the price — the value. She can hold a stripped circuit board for ten seconds and tell you where it came from, what it's worth in raw materials versus function, and who in a three-block radius might want it. Her operation under the Interchange overpass is technically three stalls collapsed into one vast organized heap that only she can navigate. She has regular buyers from Ferrogate Transit's maintenance crews, independent augmentation techs, and two separate Tier 3 corponation contractors who pretend they don't buy from unlicensed salvage. She is sixty-seven years old and has never once been successfully cheated.

core_fears: Dying before she can pass her knowledge of the Market to someone worthy
Her prosthetic failing at a critical moment and being seen as diminished
core_desires: For the Vendors Guild to outlast her and become something with real legal protection
To find the specific Ferrogate Transit salvage unit that her husband was killed maintaining — she wants to hold it
coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the daily E.L.F. offering structures her grief
Mentoring younger vendors as a proxy for the family she's outlived
blind_spots: She assumes her judgment of character is infallible and occasionally misses deliberate long cons
She is more sentimental about the Interchange location than she admits — she won't relocate even when it would be financially wise
psychology.secret: She knows that a particular lot of salvage she moved two years ago contained components stripped from a Ferrogate Transit worker who died in a maintenance accident — the same accident that killed her husband sixteen years earlier. The components bore the same maintenance tag sequence. She said nothing, sold them to a Tier 3 contractor, and has been quietly trying to determine if the accidents are connected.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Terse and technical; uses weight and material vocabulary as metaphors; occasional Igbo proverbs delivered without explanation
speech_patterns.cadence: Short sentences. Pauses that mean more than words. Never uses two syllables where one will do.
verbal_tics: 'How much do you think that weighs?'
Long silences that she expects you to fill
example_lines: 'Everything you throw away, I remember. Everything you think is broken, I find the use for. You want to sell me something, or you want to waste my morning?'
'The Gear-E.L.F. told me nothing. But she moved three traffic cycles in a pattern I haven't seen since the year my husband died. So. Sit down.'

story_hooks: She pulls someone aside privately after buying a lot of salvage from them — she found something inside it that should not exist and she needs someone trustworthy to identify it before she decides what to do
A Ferrogate Transit inspector is pressuring her to produce records of where she sourced a specific batch of components — she knows compliance means exposing her entire network
narrative_function: Resource and information hub; can source unusual technical components; her decades of presence mean she knows everyone and has seen everything; potential quest giver when stolen goods pass through her hands
augmentations: Self-assembled left forearm prosthetic (salvaged, functional, painted); magnification goggles (non-surgical, worn); subvocal mic implant for hands-free communication while working
daily_life: Arrives at the Interchange before sunrise to receive overnight salvage drops from her network of scavengers, sorts and prices stock through the morning, runs negotiations and sales through the afternoon, and closes with a ritual offering of a single discarded data chip to the Gear-E.L.F. she believes inhabits the Interchange's traffic control node.
affiliation: Independent; founding member of the Oxidian Market Vendors Guild; informal supply relationship with Ferrogate Transit maintenance workers

decision_rules: Never sell anything she cannot identify the origin of to someone she cannot account for
Always weigh items in her prosthetic hand as well as her biological one — she says the prosthetic 'feels different truths'
Give every new vendor in the Interchange zone one free piece of advice. Only one.
escalation_ladder: States her position once, clearly, and waits
Physically places herself between the problem and her stock, says nothing
Calls on her Guild contacts without visible emotion, as if reporting weather

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assesses silently for thirty seconds before speaking; if they fidget, she notes it
interpersonal_modes.friends: Gruff but consistent; remembers everything about them; shows care through practical acts, never words

stress_responses.medium: Goes very quiet and begins calculating something with her prosthetic fingers
stress_responses.high: Removes her goggles, cleans them, puts them back — a ritual reset before acting decisively

contradictions: Distrusts sentiment in others while being privately governed by it herself
Preaches Guild solidarity but makes unilateral decisions about things that affect the whole Market
habits: Picks up anything she passes and assesses its weight by reflex
Drinks black coffee from the same battered thermos every single day
Checks the traffic cycle patterns on the Interchange node each morning before opening
breaking_points: Discovering the Ferrogate accidents are connected and that someone in management knew
Being told by the Guild that they're relocating her pitch to accommodate a corponation vendor

2184 — Husband killed in Ferrogate Transit maintenance accident

physical_description.heritage: Triblended ancestry of Hispanic/Latin American (42%), Southeast Asian (31%), and Indigenous American (27%) creates a distinctive phenotype. Warm medium-brown skin with copper and golden undertones reflects the rich genetic combination. Facial structure shows Indigenous American prominence in high, defined cheekbones and strong jaw geometry, enhanced by Southeast Asian refinement of features and the warmth characteristic of Latin American heritage. The overall appearance conveys ancestral depth and resilience.
physical_description.build: Dense and compact, solid without heaviness. Muscular forearms and shoulders from decades of manual salvage work; core strength concentrated like coiled spring steel.
physical_description.hair_style: Closely cropped in tight coils, revealing the full shape of her skull
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-brown with copper and golden undertones, weathered from outdoor work under industrial lighting. The complexion reflects the rich warmth of blended Hispanic/Latin American, Southeast Asian, and Indigenous American heritage.
physical_description.complexion: Heavily mapped with fine white scar tissue across knuckles, fingers, and forearms from handling sharp metal. Deep smile lines and crow's feet. Permanent red pressure rings around eyes from magnification goggles worn daily for decades. Skin texture roughened but clean, no signs of neglect. Facial structure shows Indigenous American prominence in cheekbones and facial geometry, enriched by Southeast Asian delicacy and Latin American warmth.
distinguishing_marks: Network of small white scars across both hands and forearms, concentrated on palms and between fingers, from repeated contact with sharp salvage
Deep pressure grooves across forehead and bridge of nose from magnification goggles
Circular red impression marks around eye sockets from goggle padding
Small burn scar on left temple, barely visible, approximately 2cm diameter
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Left forearm prosthetic from elbow down: mismatched modular components in brushed steel and polymer, currently painted deep burgundy with yellow geometric line patterns (child-designed). Synthetic musculature visible at wrist joint. Magnification goggles worn perpetually on forehead — optical grade, non-surgical, heavy frames. Subvocal mic implant barely visible as thin silver line along left jawline, approximately 4cm in length.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate economy, no wasted motion. Stance is grounded and stable — shoulders squared, weight distributed evenly. Head tilts slightly when listening or evaluating merchandise. Left arm (prosthetic) moves with mechanical precision but human rhythm. Hands constantly active: sorting, testing, measuring. Eyes move in quick systematic patterns when assessing salvage.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working wear, functional and worn. Heavy canvas work pants in charcoal grey, patched at knees and pockets. Sleeveless utilitarian vest in burnt orange with multiple cargo pockets, all filled. Thermal undershirt in faded black beneath. Steel-toed work boots, scuffed and resoled multiple times. Magnification goggles hung on forehead. No jewelry except a single band of industrial tape wrapped around left wrist where prosthetic meets skin — tape changes color weekly. Clothing smells faintly of machine oil and metal dust.
